findings.title: Outage root cause #2 (the 176-273 vp RMSE): stale lastPrice is paired with Yahoo's bisection-artefact impliedVolatility, so the anchors get vega of about 1-4 instead of about 500
findings.description: cloud_refresh keeps Yahoo's `impliedVolatility` as `implied_vol` (row filter `impliedVolatility > 0.01`). When either bid or ask is <= 0 it falls back to `lastPrice` for `mid_price`. Yahoo computes impliedVolatility by bisecting on ITS OWN (bid+ask)/2, starting from lo=1e-5, hi=1 with a tolerance of about $0.005. On an empty book that mid is 0. Near-ATM and ITM lines then get IV=1e-5 and are dropped by the >0.01 filter. OTM-wing lines get 2^-k artefacts (0.0156, 0.0313, 0.0625, 0.125, 0.5) and survive. The calibrator then (a) takes the 'top-9 BS vega' anchors among those artefact rows, (b) computes vega from the artefact IV, which lands near the 0.5 floor, and (c) fits Heston to stale, non-monotone lastPrice trades. Vega-normalised errors are inflated about 150x, which produces the 176-273 vp 'SPX RMSE' in every Mon-Thu run since 2026-09-08. I ruled out the other suspects. The reported RMSE is sqrt(SPX leg)*100 only: 1.407567 = 0.4545*1.7597^2 + 0.5454*0.0066^2 + about 5e-8 Feller penalty, so there is no penalty leakage. T is computed from the spot session, so there is no T mismatch. SVI is not on the production path. No IV inversion is involved. Units are consistent. Yahoo IV is also unusable when the book is live. It carries a 1.17 vp put/call discontinuity at the same strike because Yahoo's forward is inconsistent with put-call parity.
findings.evidence: 1) Yahoo-IV emulator (bisection lo=1e-5 hi=1 tol=0.005, S=7706, r=4%) reproduces Yahoo's IV on 585/694 zero-quote rows of the live ^SPX chain fetched 2026-09-24 00:47 UTC. Artefacts occur only on OTM wings (moneyness <0.9 or >1.1); every near-ATM or ITM zero-quote row gets 1e-5. 2) Emulated empty book (bid=ask=0, Yahoo-rule IV) through the UNMODIFIED CI code: 'Saved 2163 option contracts' (CI 09-23: 2206), '9 liquid options across 1 expiries', 'SPX smile RMSE 179.83' (CI: 175.97), kappa=19.996 (pinned), v0=0.0009, sigma=1.27. The selected anchors were strikes 7410-7870 with mid=lastPrice (7565P 11.00 next to 7570P 23.28), IV 0.0156-0.0625 and bs_vega 1.0-3.6. 3) The same session's chain with live quotes (00:47 UTC) through the same CI code gives RMSE 0.10 vp. 4) CI logs: 09-10 Thu 214.61 vp (v0 0.0006, VIX RMSE 24.48), 09-21 Mon 272.61, 09-22 Tue 205.68 (v0 0.0008, VIX 17.24), 09-23 Wed 175.97. Friday runs: 09-11 RMSE 0.22 (accepted), 09-18 RMSE 0.38 (degenerate). 5) Live 2026-10-07 slice: Yahoo IV K=7705 P 10.78% vs C 11.95%. Parity-forward IV: P 11.34% vs C 11.30%. 6) Adopting only the expiry-selection fix is NOT enough: on the emulated empty book that variant still gives 6 expiries, 54 options and 'SPX RMSE 419.10 vp'.
findings.proposed_fix: In cloud_refresh, replace lines 259-281 with a clean_option_chain() step: (i) keep only two-sided quotes (bid>0, ask>0, ask>=bid, (ask-bid)/mid <= 0.35). (ii) never fall back to lastPrice. (iii) compute a per-expiry forward from put-call parity on near-ATM strikes: F = median((C_mid-P_mid)/DF + K). (iv) compute IV yourself with Black-76 on (mid, F, DF). Keep Yahoo IV only as a diagnostic column, if at all. (v) add a quote-state gate: if under 80% of |K/S-1|<3% lines in the chosen expiries are two-sided, emit ::warning:: and return without calibrating. Proof, patched copy at scratchpad/audit/livecal (diff at scratchpad/lc/livecal_fix.diff): the emulated empty book now yields 'Chain hygiene: 2948 raw -> 0 two-sided rows ... ::warning::SPX book has no live two-sided quotes' and fails closed. The live chain is accepted (see livecal-first8-expiries). Tests: a unit test feeding a bid=ask=0 chain with 2^-k IVs must return False with that reason; a unit test asserting the put/call IV at the same strike differ by less than 0.2 vp after cleaning.

findings.title: Outage root cause #1: the pipeline downloads the first 8 listed expiries, but SPX lists one per weekday, so at most one expiry survives the >=7d filter
findings.description: `exps = [e for e in (exps or [])[:8]]` takes about 1.5 weeks of daily SPXW expiries. After `_MIN_T_DAYS=7` only 7-12 day slices remain. Only the 14d bucket is within the 50% tolerance, so every run since the chain was wired in (90dc851) calibrated a 5-parameter Heston to 9 options on ONE expiry. Even with clean data this is under-identified. 09-18 (Friday, clean quotes, RMSE 0.38) collapsed to the degenerate corner (sigma=0.0011, rho=0). 09-11 (RMSE 0.22) passed the gate and is the live headline.
findings.evidence: Live ^SPX expiries at 00:47 UTC: 56 listed, starting 2026-09-24, 09-25, 09-28, 09-29, 09-30, 10-01, 10-02, 10-05. From session 09-23 those are 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 12 days. Every CI log reads '9 liquid options across 1 expiries' (09-10, 09-11, 09-18, 09-21, 09-22, 09-23). Reproduced on the live chain with the CI code: 9 options / 1 expiry, accepted at RMSE 0.10 vp, kappa 3.74, rho -0.95 pinned. PROOF OF FIX, live Yahoo chain fetched 2026-09-24 01:13 UTC with the patched pipeline (nearest listed expiry to 14/30/60/91/180/365d, clean two-sided quotes, parity forwards, delta-spread strikes, index-mapped VIX leg). Expiries selected: 2026-10-07, 10-23, 11-20, 12-18, 2027-03-19, 09-17. 2948 raw -> 2557 two-sided rows. 54 options across 6 expiries. kappa=5.2672, theta=0.04835, sigma=0.7137, rho=-0.9150, v0=0.01543. SPX RMSE 1.460 vp (true IV inversion: 1.514 vp, max 3.05). VIX index RMSE 0.668. Feller BINDING. 4 effective d.o.f. Accepted. The saved 00:47 chain gave nearly the same result (1.478 / 0.687; params within 1%). Selection fix alone (original code otherwise): 6 expiries / 54 options, SPX 0.28 vp, VIX 0.03, kappa 3.28, sigma 0.516, rho -0.95 (pinned).
findings.proposed_fix: Add select_calibration_expiries(listed, session_date): for each target in (14,30,60,91,180,365), pick the listed expiry with days>=7 nearest the target, within 50%, and unique. Download only those. Optionally also take the neighbour on each side so a bucket survives a bad slice. Keep `_CAL_EXPIRY_TARGETS_DAYS` as the single source of truth and import it from joint_calibrator. Test: given a synthetic list of daily expiries, the function returns 6 distinct expiries with |days-target| <= 0.5*target. An integration test with a fake yfinance must yield n_spx_expiries==6.

findings.title: The quality gate and the dashboard selector have no SPX data-sufficiency or freshness test, so the 9-option single-expiry 09-11 fit is the live headline and stale-surface archive fits stay eligible
findings.description: C20 (35690a2) made the VIX leg's data sufficiency a hard precondition. The SPX leg has the same failure mode (fewer data means a lower RMSE) and has no such check. is_acceptable_calibration never looks at n_spx_options or n_expiries. latest_good_calibration_path() ranks by SPX RMSE, so joint_cal_2026-09-11.pkl (n_spx_options=9, one ~14d expiry, strikes within +/-0.5%, RMSE 0.215) beats every real fit. Separately, all 29 archived pickles from 06-16 to 09-04 lack spx_snapshot_date. Commit 90dc851 states they were refits of the frozen 2026-06-20 surface with misaligned T. The freshness check exists only at write time in cloud_refresh, so these pickles remain selectable. The 07-01 headline that C20 chose was one of them.
findings.evidence: Selector run in the copy: 'SELECTED: .../joint_cal_2026-09-11.pkl'. The pickle dump shows n_spx_options=9, n_vix_tenors=4, spx_snapshot_date='2026-09-11'. Live https://navnoorbawa.me/calibration.html reads 'Fit from 9 SPX options and 4 VIX tenors, all taken on the closed SPX session of 2026-09-11'. Pickles 06-16 through 09-04 all print snap=None. A strict selector (acceptable AND n_expiries>=4 AND spx_snapshot_date==spot_date, with 03-24 and 05-31 whitelisted as fitted on their own chain) headlines joint_cal_2026-05-31.pkl (0.523 vp) until a valid new fit exists.
findings.proposed_fix: Persist n_spx_expiries, plus min/max moneyness per expiry, in the result. Extend is_acceptable_calibration(params, spx_rmse, n_vix_tenors, n_spx_expiries, n_spx_options) to reject n_spx_expiries < 4 or n_spx_options < 30. For legacy pickles without n_spx_expiries, use n_spx_options < 30. In latest_good_calibration_path, also require cal['spx_snapshot_date'] == cal['spot_date'] (explicit legacy whitelist for 03-24 and 05-31). Rank by RMSE only among fits using the SAME anchor rule. Tests: a selector test with fixture pickles (9-option fresh, 54-option stale, 54-option fresh) must pick the 54-option fresh one. Assert that the gate rejects n_spx_expiries=1 with a reason string.

findings.title: The VIX leg compares forward-start model VIX futures with spot-start VIX indices: the published '0.03-0.27 VIX RMSE' hides a 2.7-3.1 VIX-point miss
findings.description: _vix_futures_leg calls heston_vix_futures_curve(tenors). That is sqrt of the expected variance over the 30-day window [T, T+30d]. It is compared with ^VIX9D, ^VIX, ^VIX3M and ^VIX6M, which are SPOT-start windows [0, tau]. For those indices Heston has an exact closed form with no proxy needed: VIX_tau^2 = theta + (v0-theta)(1-e^{-kappa tau})/(kappa tau), which is heston_integrated_variance(tau). The current mapping lets the model match the index levels with a spot variance far below the market's, so the published 'VIX futures RMSE' is not a measure of the model's fit to the VIX curve. The downloader comment 'VIX_futures(T) ≈ VIX_Td(today)' is the source of the error. The calibrator also uses 91d for ^VIX3M while the downloader tags it 93d.
findings.evidence: At the live headline params (09-11: kappa 5.00, theta 0.0431, sigma 0.657, v0 0.01088), the model quantities used in the loss are [14.05, 16.00, 18.85, 20.24]. The model's true index levels are [11.31, 12.92, 15.72, 17.68]. The market on 09-11 was [14.47, 15.84, 18.60, 20.39]. So the model ^VIX is 12.92 against a market 15.84, while the site reports VIX RMSE 0.27. On today's chain (market 09-23: 13.45/15.18/18.11/20.11), the CI-code fit reports RMSE 0.08 but its true index RMSE is 2.89. The selection-only fit reports 0.03, true 2.72. With the index mapping the fit reaches 0.69 (params kappa 5.27, rho -0.915, v0 0.0154, i.e. 12.4% vol, closer to VIX9D 13.45). Ablation on today's chain with clean data: futures mapping + delta-spread strikes gives kappa 2.92, sigma 0.53, rho -0.87, VIX 0.37 (true index error not shown). Index mapping gives kappa 5.22, sigma 0.71, rho -0.91.
findings.proposed_fix: In _vix_futures_leg (and validate()), set model = 100*sqrt(heston_integrated_variance(tau, kappa, theta, v0)) for each index tenor. Use 93/365 for VIX3M to match the downloader. Rename the leg 'VIX term-structure (index) leg' in the code, dashboard and README. Update test_vix_leg_zero_at_exact_fit so its exact-fit target is built with the same index formula. In the patched copy it is the only one of 73 targeted tests that fails, as expected. If real VIX futures are ever sourced, keep heston_vix_futures_curve for THAT leg only.

findings.title: 'Top-9 by BS vega' with OTM-vs-spot anchors every expiry in a 0.5-3% call-side sliver: no puts at >=30-58d, so the SPX skew is never fitted
findings.description: BS vega peaks at K ≈ S·exp((r-q+σ²/2)T), above spot, and the OTM filter is relative to SPOT. As a result the 9 highest-vega strikes of every slice are ATM or slightly OTM calls. The 'joint SPX/VIX smile calibration' therefore never sees the put wing that identifies rho and vol-of-vol. That explains rho pinned at -0.95 on almost every archived fit, the degenerate corner on 09-18, and the misleadingly low RMSEs. The dashboard's 'Moneyness lo 0.70' is irrelevant because the selected anchors never reach it.
findings.evidence: Original code, 2026-05-31 showcase snapshot (S=7580): the 15d bucket has 6 puts at 0.9927-1.0092. Buckets 30/61/92/173/355d have 0 puts, moneyness 1.0007-1.0059, 1.0046-1.0099, 1.0079-1.0145, 1.0092-1.0356 and 1.0389-1.0653. The 2026-03-24 snapshot and today's chain show the same pattern (today's 359d bucket: calls at 1.038-1.064). The patched rule (9 strikes nearest z = ln(K/F)/(σ_atm√T) in linspace(-2.5,1.5,9), OTM vs forward) covers 0.947-1.035 at 14d and 0.701-1.298 at 359d, with 5-6 puts per expiry. Result: rho -0.915 (not pinned), true-IV RMSE 1.51 vp, i.e. Heston's genuine short-dated skew misfit (1.28 vp at 14d, 1.88 vp at 359d) instead of a flattering 0.1-0.5 vp.
findings.proposed_fix: Pick anchors on a standardized-moneyness or delta grid per expiry: e.g. z in [-2.5, 1.5], or put deltas 10/20/30/40 plus call deltas 40/25/10. Decide OTM against the parity forward, not spot. Keep vega-normalised weights. Update the dashboard 'Vega-weighted anchor selection' step and README accordingly. Re-publish the RMSE claims, which will rise to about 1.5 vp. That rise is the honest number. Test: for any expiry the selected anchors must include at least 3 puts with K/F < 0.97 whenever such quotes exist.

findings.title: The calibration uses hard-coded r=4.5%, q=1.3% while the pickle and dashboard publish r=^IRX (3.91%) and q=0.0%: displayed inputs are not those used, and the flat carry biases 1y IVs by 1.2-1.9 vp
findings.description: `JointCalibrator(as_of_date=TODAY)` runs with the defaults r=0.045 and q=0.013. cloud_refresh then overwrites result['r'] with get_tbill_rate() and never stores q. The site shows 'Risk-free rate r 3.91% USD 6M SOFR (2026-03)' and 'Dividend yield q 0.0%', yet the fit used 4.5% and 1.3%. The label is also wrong: the value is the ^IRX 3M bill, not 6M SOFR, and not from 2026-03. The market's own carry, implied from put-call parity, runs from about 2.3% at 1-2w to 4.0-4.2% at 6-12m versus the hard-coded 3.2%. That shifts the 1y forward by about 75 index points. The ^IRX discount yield is also not converted to continuous compounding (4.03% discount ≈ 4.11% cc).
findings.evidence: Live page text: 'Risk-free rate r 3.91% USD 6M SOFR (2026-03) Dividend yield q 0.0%'. The 09-11 pickle has r=0.03913 and no q key. Parity regression on the live chain gives F(7d)=7709.5, F(30d)=7727.0, F(189d)=7867.1 and F(372d)=8037.8 against S=7706.03, i.e. implied r-q of 0.023, 0.033, 0.040 and 0.041. Black-76 at T=359d with σ=0.19: pricing with carry 3.2% against a true 4.14% biases call IVs by +1.94/+1.49/+1.19 vp at K=7300/7706/8100, with puts biased the opposite way through parity. Parity also absorbs GTH drift: q_14d moved from 1.69% to 2.42% between the 00:47 and 01:13 UTC fetches.
findings.proposed_fix: Pass r to JointCalibrator: r_cc = -ln(1 - d·91/360)/(91/365) from ^IRX d. Replace the scalar q with per-expiry q_T = r - ln(F_T/S)/T from parity forwards, as the patch does (self.q_by_T, used in _spx_leg and in vega). Persist r, q_by_expiry and the forwards in the pickle. Dashboard: show 'r (3M T-bill ^IRX, session date)' and the implied carry per tenor. Remove the 'USD 6M SOFR (2026-03)' label. Test: for a synthetic chain priced off known F_T, the calibrator recovers q_T to 1e-4 and _spx_leg is about 0 at the generating params.

findings.title: The daily cron reliably lands in the Mon-Thu window when Cboe's SPX book is empty (after the 17:00 ET curb close, before GTH quotes at about 20:30 ET), and its timing rationale rests on a false 'no history' premise
findings.description: The cron is scheduled at 22:00 UTC. GitHub starts it 87-138 min late, i.e. 23:27-00:18 UTC = 19:27-20:18 EDT. Cboe runs RTH to 16:15, curb to 17:00, then Global Trading Hours from 20:15 ET, with the GTH queuing period from 20:00. Yahoo data is 15-min delayed. Every Mon-Thu run therefore sampled a book without two-sided quotes. Friday evenings have no GTH session, so the closing quotes persist, and those were exactly the runs with sane RMSE (0.22, 0.38). Placing the job before about 04:00 UTC was justified by 'VIX9D/3M/6M exist on Yahoo ONLY as a current-day row (no history)'. That premise is false today: Yahoo serves full daily history, including the dates the README calls 1-tenor days. So the job can move to a window with a live book.
findings.evidence: Run created_at (UTC): 09-09 23:33, 09-10 23:27, 09-11 23:34 (Fri, accepted), 09-15 00:01, 09-15 23:46, 09-16 23:54, 09-17 23:45, 09-18 23:40 (Fri, clean data), 09-22 00:18, 09-22 23:52, 09-24 00:01. At 00:50 UTC, live quotes change minute to minute: 121/366, 144/422 and 322/946 lines changed between fetches 3 min apart, while lastPrice was unchanged. That confirms GTH quotes are live then. Cboe: GTH 8:15pm-9:25am ET, curb 4:15-5:00pm ET, GTH queuing from 8:00pm ET. yf.Ticker('^VIX9D'/'^VIX3M'/'^VIX6M').history(2026-09-01..09-24) returns 15 rows each. The DB after refresh holds 274 rows per sub-tenor from 2025-08-20 to 2026-09-23. Full 4-tenor rows exist for the '1-tenor' days 07-14, 07-23, 08-19, 08-25 and 08-28.
findings.proposed_fix: Split the job. Keep 22:00 UTC for market data and labels. Run the options/calibration step on '30 1 * * 2-6', plus a retry at '30 3 * * 2-6'. After GitHub's delay these land in GTH (about 22:00-01:00 ET) or, on Saturday, in the Friday-close book, and the existing 'pickle exists' check makes the retry idempotent. Keep the two-sided-quote gate from livecal-yahoo-iv-lastprice-pairing so a mistimed run fails closed. Use parity forwards so GTH spot drift does not bias the fit. Correct the workflow comment and README lines 124-126. Optionally backfill the archived 1-tenor fits now that the history exists. Test: a small script run on a schedule logs the two-sided share, and the gate unit test covers the empty-book case.

findings.title: The job reports success while no calibration was produced for 13 of 14 runs: no warning, no step summary, no exit code, no retained evidence, and no staleness banner on the site
findings.description: recalibrate_heston() returns False, but __main__ ignores the return value, and the rejection is logged at WARNING inside a green job. Nothing records the rejected chain. The DB is not committed and the options parquet mirror is not uploaded, so a root cause cannot be recovered after the fact. That is why the exact 176-vp inputs are not recoverable and had to be reconstructed by emulation. The site header shows 'Calibration: 2026-09-11' with no age or last-attempt status, 8 sessions stale as of today.
findings.evidence: All 12 runs from 81 to 92 have conclusion=success. Only 09-11 produced a pickle. Run 92 log: 'Calibration REJECTED (SPX RMSE too high (175.97vp > 3.0))' followed by 'Refresh complete'. The workflow git-adds only regime_labels.parquet and joint_cal_*.pkl and has no actions/upload-artifact step. index.html:11 renders the bare date.
findings.proposed_fix: 1) cloud_refresh writes data_store/calibrations/last_attempt.json on every run and the workflow commits it. Fields: session, run_utc, status accepted/rejected/skipped, reason, n_raw, n_two_sided, two_sided_share, expiries, n_spx_expiries, n_spx_options, spx_rmse, vix_rmse, params. 2) Print '::warning title=Calibration rejected::<reason>' or '::notice::' and append a Markdown table to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY. 3) Add a final workflow step `python scripts/check_calibration_freshness.py --max-sessions 3`, with if: always(), after the deploy. It counts spx_ohlcv sessions after the newest accepted pickle and exits 1 when there are more than 3, so the run turns red and GitHub emails the owner while the site still deploys. 4) Upload data_store/parquet/options_spx_<session>.parquet plus the diagnostics JSON with actions/upload-artifact@v4 (retention 30d). 5) Dashboard: when the newest accepted fit is more than 2 sessions old, show an amber banner on / and /calibration: 'Heston calibration from 2026-09-11 (8 sessions old). Last attempt 2026-09-23 rejected: <reason>'. Tests: unit-test the freshness script on fixture pickles and spx dates (exit 0/1). Add a freeze_site test asserting the banner text when the fixture is stale.

findings.title: The rejected or garbage chain is written to options_snapshots before calibrating and never removed; get_options_surface later serves it with stale T
findings.description: insert_options_snapshot runs before the calibration and the quality gate, and the rejection branch returns without deleting the rows or the parquet mirror. In CI this is ephemeral because the DB is not committed. Locally, and in any process sharing the DB, the rejected snapshot becomes 'the most recent snapshot <= as_of_date' for every later caller that lacks cloud_refresh's freshness guard (QuinticCalibrator, research code, tests). get_options_surface returns the snapshot's stored time_to_expiry, measured from the snapshot date, without checking that the snapshot matches the as_of session. vol_system.db is git-tracked, so a local run followed by a commit would ship the garbage.
findings.evidence: After the empty-book run in scratch copy livecal_a, the DB holds 1454 rows for session 2026-09-23 with bid=ask=0 in all of them, and data_store/parquet/options_spx_2026-09-23.parquet exists. db.get_options_surface('2026-10-05','SPX') serves 'snapshot 2026-09-23 rows 1454 min stored T days 14 (expiry 2026-10-07)'. The true T on 10-05 is 2 days.
findings.proposed_fix: Write the chain to a staging table, or with a status column (quality='pending'), inside one transaction. Promote it to accepted only after the gate passes, and on rejection DELETE it or mark it 'rejected' and exclude it in get_options_surface. Make get_options_surface return time_to_expiry recomputed from as_of_date, or raise or flag when snapshot_date is not the as_of session. Tests: a rejected cloud_refresh run leaves zero SPX rows for that session, and a get_options_surface call with as_of later than the snapshot returns T measured from as_of.

findings.title: If the market-data refresh fails, the options step still runs against the last DB session and stores today's chain under that old session label with T off by months
findings.description: __main__ continues after `market_ok=False`. recalibrate_heston takes spot_date from whatever SPX row is newest in the DB (the committed DB ends 2026-06-18), downloads the live chain, labels it as that session, and computes T from it. It also never checks that latest_session_date is actually closed: a workflow_dispatch during RTH would label an intraday bar as the session and the evening cron would then skip it. Today the stale check happened to catch the case only because an even newer June snapshot (06-20) exists in the committed DB.
findings.evidence: Fresh copy of the committed DB, market refresh skipped, today's chain served: '[3/4] Downloading SPX options for session 2026-06-18 (run date 2026-09-24)' then 'Saved 3465 option contracts as the 2026-06-18 SPX snapshot' and 'SPX spot S = 7500.58 (date: 2026-06-18)'. The fit was rejected only by 'SPX surface is stale (snapshot 2026-06-20, session 2026-06-18)'. The mislabelled rows remain in the DB.
findings.proposed_fix: Skip the options step unless market_ok is true AND spot_date is the most recent completed NYSE session. Use a check such as now_ET > spot_date 16:15 ET and spot_date >= previous business day (pandas_market_calendars or a holiday list), or cross-check Yahoo's ^SPX regularMarketTime. Test: with the SPX download mocked empty, recalibrate_heston returns False with an explicit reason and writes nothing.

findings.title: The disabled VIX-options leg is internally inconsistent (put via Jensen-biased parity forward, vega on spot VIX, stale 3-month-old snapshot), so the published '37.14 vp = structural failure of the CIR density' is unsupported
findings.description: heston_vix_put_price derives puts by parity from sqrt(E[VIX^2]), while the call comes from the exact CIR density. The forward used should be E[VIX_T] from that same density. This makes put prices wrong by about 0.7-1.0 VIX points and sometimes negative. _prepare_vix_options computes vega and moneyness from SPOT VIX rather than the VIX future for that expiry. It also reads the latest VIX snapshot (2026-06-20) with its stored T and no freshness check. Those stale contracts still toggle the weight renormalisation (0.50/0.60 versus 0.45/0.55) and are recorded as n_vix_options=6 in the 09-11 provenance. The dashboard and config nevertheless attribute the 37.14 vp VIX-options RMSE to a structural CIR-density failure.
findings.evidence: At today's selection-only params (kappa 3.28, theta 0.0462, sigma 0.516, v0 0.0116), T=30d: E[VIX_T]=14.521 while sqrt(E[VIX^2])=15.183. The put for K=12/15/18 is 0.003/1.392/3.472 from the code versus 0.670/2.058/4.137 from the density (err -0.67). At T=60d, K=12 the code gives -0.383, a negative price, against 0.567. The 09-10 CI log shows 'VIX options: 7 liquid contracts' and 'Weights: w1=0.50, w2=0.60'. The 09-23 log shows 0 contracts and w1=0.45, w2=0.55.
findings.proposed_fix: Price VIX puts by integrating max(K-VIX,0) against the same density, or use parity with E[VIX_T] computed from it. Compute vega and moneyness on the model or market VIX future for each expiry. Require VIX-options snapshot_date == spot_date, else leave the leg empty. Normalise weights independently of the stale leg. Re-measure before claiming a 'structural' failure. Test: put-call parity holds to 1e-6 with the density forward, and the put is non-negative for K in [5, 60].

findings.title: The dashboard, README and site meta advertise 'SVI/SSVI smoothing: calibrate Heston to smooth surface ... butterfly-free', but _build_ssvi_surface is never called in production
findings.description: The only callers of _fit_svi_slice and _build_ssvi_surface are tests. The calibrator docstring itself says 'Direct calibration against market quotes (no SVI pre-smoothing)'. The code is per-slice raw SVI, not SSVI. It is explicitly not butterfly-free (g(k) is not enforced), and it has no calendar check despite the comment 'Calendar-spread guard'. It evaluates IV at unclipped k but emits the clipped K, and it assigns C/P against spot rather than the forward. Its success tolerance (MSE < 1e-3 in total variance) is meaningless for short slices.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn '_build_ssvi_surface\|_fit_svi_slice' --include=*.py` returns only joint_calibrator.py:309 (internal) and tests/test_joint_calibrator.py. dashboard/app.py:1098 step 3 claims 'Fit Gatheral (2004) SVI per expiry; calibrate Heston to smooth surface not noisy quotes ... Butterfly-free surface.'
findings.proposed_fix: Either remove the SVI/SSVI claims (dashboard step 3, README C13 row, og/meta descriptions, make_og_image chips), or wire in a real SSVI (Gatheral-Jacquier 2014) with the butterfly condition g(k)>=0 and calendar monotonicity checked, applied before anchor selection, and document it. Test: when wired in, an integration test asserts the calibrator calls the smoother and that g(k)>=0 on the output grid.

findings.title: Monthly expiries mix AM-settled SPX and PM-settled SPXW lines at different strikes, all priced with a single PM-close T
findings.description: For third-Friday expiries Yahoo returns one line per strike, some with the SPX (AM, SOQ-settled) root and some with the SPXW (PM) root. The pipeline drops the contract symbol and assigns every line T=(expiry-session)/365. AM lines expire about 6.5h earlier, and their settlement (SOQ) differs from the 16:00 close. The bias is small but systematic within the monthly slices the tenor selector prefers (30d, 58d, 177d, 359d).
findings.evidence: Live 2026-10-16 slice: SPX261016C07695000, SPX261016C07700000 and SPX261016C07705000 next to SPXW261016C07710000. SPX-root lines carry OI>0 6.3% of the time versus 2.7% for SPXW. No (expiry,strike,right) appears with both roots.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep contractSymbol (or root) in options_snapshots. Prefer SPXW lines. Where only AM lines exist, set T to the 09:30 ET settlement time, or drop them in favour of the nearest PM expiry. Test: the clean_option_chain output has a single root per expiry, or root-specific T.

findings.title: Cosmetic provenance defects: the gh-pages commit message contains a literal '$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)', and the calibrator logs and prints the run date (09-24) for a fit of the 09-23 session
findings.description: Action `with:` inputs are not shell-expanded, so every gh-pages commit is titled 'Deploy <id>: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)'. JointCalibrator is built with as_of_date=TODAY, the UTC run date, so the CI log reads 'Joint calibration: 2026-09-24' and 'Calibrated Heston Parameters (2026-09-24)' for the 2026-09-23 session. That is confusing during incident triage. Functionally, get_options_surface also filters `expiry > run date`.
findings.evidence: Run 92 log: '[gh-pages 83633b4] Deploy 35936484677: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d) ef47f93...' and '── Calibrated Heston Parameters (2026-09-24) ──' directly after 'Downloading SPX options for session 2026-09-23'.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute the date in a prior step (`echo "today=$(date -u +%F)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT`) and use ${{ steps.x.outputs.today }}. Construct JointCalibrator(as_of_date=spot_date) so logs, filters and the pickle all use the session. Test: none needed beyond checking the log line.

checked_ok: Reported SPX RMSE = sqrt(SPX leg)*100 only; Feller penalty and 1e6 out-of-bounds returns do not leak into it. Verified from run 92: 1.407567 ≈ 0.4545*1.7597^2 + 0.5454*0.0066^2 + about 5e-8 penalty. Weight renormalisation (0.5/0.6 -> 0.4545/0.5454) is correct.

time_to_expiry in cloud_refresh is measured from the spot session (not the run date), so it is consistent with S; no T mismatch caused the 176 vp. The as_of_date=TODAY run-date filter only removes the next-day expiry.
Units: Yahoo IV is decimal; mid prices and S are in index points; the vega normalisation is dimensionally correct.
No filter depends on openInterest or volume (grep of cloud_refresh/joint_calibrator); Yahoo SPX OI is 0 on 96% of lines, so any such filter would have been fatal.
SVI smoothing is not on the production path, so it cannot cause an SVI blow-up; no IV inversion happens inside the loss.
The stale-snapshot write-time guard (spx_snapshot_date != spot_date) works: it caught the June snapshot in the market-data-outage simulation.
The VIX term-structure leg is pinned to the spot session: 4 tenors on 09-23 in both CI and the reproduction. The C20 exclusive-end-date fix is effective.
DELETE-before-INSERT prevents duplicate snapshot rows on reruns; the data_store/vol_system.db changes are not committed by CI (only regime_labels.parquet and joint_cal_*.pkl are git-added).

heston_integrated_variance closed form (theta + (v0-theta)(1-e^{-kT})/(kT)) is correct; heston_call_batch is accurate enough: vega-approx RMSE 1.46 vs true-IV-inversion RMSE 1.51 vp on the fixed 54-option surface.
Reproduction fidelity: my 2026-09-24 00:47 UTC market refresh matched CI counts exactly (274 SPX, 276 VIX, 1372 VIX-TS, 274 T-bill rows; S=7706.03).

Fix proof is reproducible: the fetch at 00:47 UTC and the live Yahoo fetch at 01:13 UTC give params within about 1% and SPX RMSE 1.478 vs 1.460 vp; the patched copy passes 72/73 targeted tests, and the one failure is the intended VIX-leg mapping test that must be updated.

The shared repo /home/user/vol-system-dashboard was not modified (git status clean). All runs were done in scratchpad/audit/livecal, livecal_a and livecal_b; the proof diff is at scratchpad/lc/livecal_fix.diff and the saved live chain at scratchpad/lc/spx_chain_raw.parquet.
